steps.title: Welcome to Your Studio
steps.content: This is the home page where you can see a summary of all your projects.

steps.title: Project Stats
steps.content: Here you can see (1) the total amount of projects your studio has, (2) how many are in progress, and (3) how many are completed.

steps.title: Project Pipeline
steps.content: This shows (1) the projects in each stage at a glance and (2) your most recent projects for quick access.

steps.title: Go to Projects
steps.content: Up next is the Projects tab. Click on it to proceed.

steps.title: Projects Library
steps.content: This is where all of your projects are created and stored. Go ahead, try creating a new project.

steps.title: Create Project Dialog
steps.content: The project creation dialog is not mandatory to fill out. If you don't have a name for the project yet, and just want to brainstorm, you can leave the title empty. Just select whether you are thinking of a long-form video or a short video and create the project.

steps.title: Idea Tab
steps.content: As you can see when creating a project, we land on the Idea tab. It's always useful to have a place to note down your brainstorming. Write down your ideas, plan your hook, think about what will keep viewers watching, and decide what your call to action will be.

steps.title: Voice to Text
steps.content: You can also use "Voice" if you are not a fan of writing manually. This is a simple voice-to-text feature that helps people who prefer speaking their ideas out loud instead of typing them.

steps.title: Why Idea First
steps.content: Something most YouTubers do wrong is jumping right into scriptwriting, recording, and editing. But just like the idea phase is important, even more crucial is to do the packaging first, before writing a single word of your script.

steps.title: Go to Packaging
steps.content: Go ahead and open the packaging tab.

steps.title: Packaging Sections
steps.content: The packaging tab has two main areas: (1) the Sets section where you create title and thumbnail combinations, and (2) the Metadata section for video description and tags.

steps.title: Multiple Sets
steps.content: You can make up to 6 different sets of titles and thumbnails. When making a video, you want to test it as much as possible to ensure it is something people will want to watch.

steps.title: Create a Set
steps.content: For now, create a simple title, and add any image as a thumbnail. It is for testing purposes only, you can change it later.

steps.title: Go to Preview
steps.content: Once you have made at least one set, move on to the preview tab.

steps.title: Preview Tab
steps.content: In the preview, you can see how your set will look on the YouTube platform.

steps.title: Compare Feature
steps.content: If you want to compare your thumbnail to your live competition, enable the compare feature. It uses the title of the set to search and show other videos so you can see exactly how your video might look next to them.

steps.title: Feed vs Suggested
steps.content: You can see how your video will look on the home feed, but also in the suggested videos section. Go ahead, click on "Suggested" to switch views.

steps.title: Desktop vs Mobile
steps.content: You can also preview how it looks on different devices. Click on "Mobile" to see the mobile view.

steps.title: Try All Combinations
steps.content: Don't forget, mobile also has feed and suggested. Try them both to make sure your thumbnail looks great everywhere.

steps.title: Go to Storyboard
steps.content: Once you have tested several thumbnails, found the one you like the most, and you are certain that this is something that people will want to click on, move on to the storyboard tab.

steps.title: Storyboard
steps.content: This is the storyboard. It is very user-friendly and simple, but extremely important for making good videos. Most people write their script then go straight to recording and editing. This is a trap that has made many YouTubers exhausted and eventually led them to quit.

steps.title: Scene Structure
steps.content: Each scene has two parts: (1) the Script where you write what you'll say, and (2) the Editor Notes where you describe what should be shown on screen while that part is being read.

steps.title: Why Editor Notes
steps.content: The process that big creators use is, while writing the script, to also write what exactly should be shown on screen. That way, all the editor (even if that's still you) has to do is simply add the elements mentioned in the editor notes.

steps.title: Managing Scenes
steps.content: You can (1) add more scenes, (2) reorder them with the arrows, or (3) delete them. Click any of these buttons to continue.

steps.title: Duration & Completion
steps.content: The storyboard also shows (1) approximately how long each scene will take, and (2) you can mark sections as complete so you know where you left off.

steps.title: Go to Board
steps.content: These are the most important parts of your project. There's also tasks, but we will see those same tasks in the Board page. Go ahead, open it.

steps.title: Board Overview
steps.content: This is where all your projects are tracked into stages. Blueprint has the most crucial stages by default.

steps.title: Edit Board
steps.content: With the edit button you can add, delete or edit stages, as well as the default tasks in each stage.

steps.title: Moving Projects
steps.content: You can see your active project here. By dragging and dropping, you can change the current stage that your project is in. Go ahead, move it to the "Package" stage.

steps.title: Project Tasks
steps.content: If you click on the project it opens the stages with the tasks for each stage that you can check as completed as you go. These are the default suggested tasks, but you can change them to fit your exact process.

steps.title: Assignees
steps.content: If you work in a team you can assign people to the project, or the individual stages.

steps.title: Deadlines
steps.content: You can also set a deadline for the entire project, and for individual stages.

steps.title: Go to Wiki
steps.content: You can now close the project tasks, and open up the Wiki page.

steps.title: Wiki Overview
steps.content: The Wiki is a simple concept but it is crucial to ensuring not only easy access to all of your important resources, but also to maintaining your branding so that your viewers get used to your style and always recognize your videos.

steps.title: Create a Document
steps.content: Here you can create a document, or a folder and create documents in it. Go ahead and try it out. Click "Create Document" and name it something like "Brand Fonts".

steps.title: Document Editor
steps.content: This is the document editor. Here you can keep things like the font you use on your thumbnails, text captions, links to sound effects, or background songs you want to use in your videos.

steps.title: Go to Settings
steps.content: Then we have the settings tab. Please open it.

steps.title: Settings Tabs
steps.content: Here we have three settings sections: Studio, Members, and Billing.

steps.title: Studio Profile
steps.content: In the Studio Profile section you can update your studio icon, name and url slug.

steps.title: Transfer Ownership
steps.content: You can transfer the studio to another user if needed.

steps.title: Tutorial & Help
steps.content: You can rerun this very tutorial anytime from here.

steps.title: Danger Zone
steps.content: And you can delete the entire studio. Be careful with this - it's permanent!

steps.title: Go to Members
steps.content: Move on to the members settings.

steps.title: Members Settings
steps.content: Here you can see the members, their roles and you can invite, remove members or edit their roles, if you have the permission for it.

steps.title: Go to Board
steps.content: Next, let's check out the Board settings.

steps.title: Board Settings
steps.content: This is where you customize your workflow. You can add, edit, rename, or reorder the default tasks that appear in every new project. Drag tasks to change their order, or double-click to rename them.

steps.title: Go to Billing
steps.content: And last is the billing settings. Open it up.

steps.title: Billing Overview
steps.content: Here you can see your billing overview, such as your current billing cycle, and the upcoming one (if there is one).

steps.title: Plans
steps.content: You can see the plan options and what they include as well as the prices. Keep in mind, yearly subscriptions are 17% cheaper.

steps.title: Redeem Code
steps.content: Here you can use a key if you have one to obtain a gifted subscription.

steps.title: Your Profile
steps.content: Finally, there is your profile. Click on it now. From here you can go back to the hub where you have the list of your studios, open your account settings, access the help center, enable or disable invites, and sign out.

steps.title: That's All!
steps.content: That's all for now. Go ahead and get started on your first project.
